why: Compare must check prerequisites in the environment it was HANDED, not the ambient one. In production those are the same object, which is exactly why dropping `deps.env ??` reads as a harmless simplification -- and why every test that injects a fake `inspectPrerequisites` is blind to it, since a fake ignores the argument. MEASURED: 1 of the 28 tests in orchestrate.test.ts fails, 'spends nothing when a real prerequisite check meets a genuinely missing FFmpeg'. That case stubs the AMBIENT PATH with working shims and passes a short-an-FFmpeg PATH through `deps.env`, so the two disagree deliberately: the mutant reads the working one, gets past the check, and reaches `resolveRef`. Stubbing the ambient PATH rather than trusting the real one is what makes this a measurement -- on a machine with no FFmpeg installed the mutant would refuse for the right reason by accident and survive. Against the pre-existing tests for this file it SURVIVES.
killedBy: compareRefs against a really broken toolchain spends nothing when a real prerequisite check meets a genuinely missing FFmpeg
